caption.text:
Comment "DEEPSEEK" to get DeepSeek Harness and build your own custom AI agent.

DeepSeek just launched their own free version of Claude Code.

It has already crossed 180k stars on GitHub in under a week.

It's called DeepSeek Harness.

Unlike Claude Code, it's fully customizable.

It's built on the idea that everything inside it is a plugin.

Including the model, the tools, the memory, and even the agent loop itself.

So you just swap out whatever piece you want.

You can build your own custom AI agent from scratch, piece by piece, exactly how you imagine it.

Which means you can run it with any AI model locally, without depending on one single provider.

You can even call Claude Code and Codex as sub agents inside it, letting different tools handle different parts of the job.

Plus it comes with 53 tools right out of the box, so you're not starting from an empty setup.

And it's completely free and open source.

Think of it like Lego blocks for AI agents, every single piece is swappable, removable, and replaceable.

Most tools lock you into their own model and their own logic, no matter what you actually need.

This one hands you the entire architecture and lets you rebuild it however you want, from the ground up.

#deepseek #deepseekharness #claudecode #aiagent #opensourceai

caption.text:
The model isn’t the entire AI system.

Everything is becoming a plugin.

Search? Plug it in.
Code execution? Plug it in.
Memory, retrieval, validation, specialized tools, or even a better model? Swap them in without rebuilding everything.

The harness is the real control layer.

It decides what gets called, when it gets called, what context it receives, and where the result goes next.

The future of AI products may not belong to whoever owns one perfect model.

It may belong to whoever builds the best system for orchestrating interchangeable components.

Everything is a plugin.
And that might be the architecture.

Save this for your next AI project and follow @DeepOnAI.labs for visual AI engineering explainers.

caption.text:
Comment “HARNESS” and I’ll send it over. 👇

DeepSeek open-sourced its own Claude Code. Then shipped it with a CLAUDE.md inside. 🐋

DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is an agent runtime — the layer that turns a model into an agent that reads files, runs commands and keeps working. Dropped Aug 13 alongside DeepSeek-V4-Pro. MIT licensed. Real repo, real deepseek-ai org.

What’s actually in it:
🔌 Everything is a plugin — models, tools, skills, sessions, sandboxes, storage, the agent loop, even the UI. All swappable from config
⚡ One command: npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web — local Web UI on 127.0.0.1:3080
🧠 Ships an AGENTS.md written so agents can read the codebase themselves
⭐ 130k+ stars, 13k forks, under a week old
⚠️ v0.1 developer preview — breaking changes are promised, not hinted

Three things the viral posts got wrong:
❌ “Free replacement for the $200 plan” — the harness is free, the model isn’t. Bring your own API key, and V4-Pro pricing went UP on Aug 16, not down
❌ “Built on Cordis, DeepSeek’s own runtime” — Cordis is a third-party open-source kernel. DeepSeek vendored it
❌ The benchmarks are DeepSeek’s own runs. No independent reproduction yet

And the detail nobody screenshotted: the repo root ships a .claude folder and a CLAUDE.md.

The Claude Code killer has a CLAUDE.md in it. That’s not a killer. That’s a standard. 🎯

Comment “HARNESS” — repo link and the honest breakdown in your DMs. 👇
